t: A federation of seven sovereign provinces, formed in the revolt against Philip II of Spain and governed from The Hague.
Its Baltic trade, East India Company and Amsterdam bank made it Europe’s leading commercial power in the 17th century.
Rembrandt, Vermeer, Spinoza and Grotius worked there; wars and British rivalry wore it down until France conquered it in 1795.
dyk: In 1628 Piet Heyn of the Dutch West India Company captured an entire Spanish silver fleet off Matanzas in Cuba, a haul that paid the company’s shareholders a large dividend.
ev: The northern provinces form the Union of Utrecht
The Act of Abjuration renounces Philip II of Spain
The Dutch East India Company (VOC) is founded
The Twelve Years’ Truce with Spain begins; the Bank of Amsterdam opens
Spain recognises Dutch independence in the Peace of Münster
Disaster Year: France and England invade and the de Witt brothers are lynched
Stadtholder William III invades England and becomes its king
French armies overrun the Republic and the Batavian Republic is proclaimed

f.capital: The Hague (seat of the States General); Amsterdam the commercial capital
